subject.title: [Feature]: Configure the shared pairing reply with a global template

question: Should OpenClaw add a global free-form pairing reply template, and may operators intentionally omit the sender ID or CLI approval instruction from it?
rationale: The missing capability is confirmed, but accepting another global config surface and defining which security-relevant pairing details are optional are product and security-policy choices rather than mechanical bug fixes.

options.title: Approve bounded global template
options.body: Add the proposed global template with deterministic placeholders, an unchanged default, explicit documentation, and tests proving pairing authorization semantics are unaffected.

options.title: Expose structured presentation fields
options.body: Permit selected labels and visibility switches instead of arbitrary templates, trading localization flexibility for tighter control over required pairing information.

options.title: Keep fixed core copy
options.body: Decline new configuration and retain the current shared message, accepting that white-label and localized deployments require external customization.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded global template
recommendation.body: Add the proposed global template with deterministic placeholders, an unchanged default, explicit documentation, and tests proving pairing authorization semantics are unaffected.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily whether this new global user-facing configuration belongs in OpenClaw core.
